strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#49631-related bug: casting a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray to Sparse[int64] or Sparse[bool] takes the target default fill_value (0/False) instead of converting the source datetimelike fill_value. Build pandas from the buggy commit 6ce79779b18c in editable mode and run the developer's new parametrized tests in pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_astype.py; they should fail on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed one.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era table entry, so no version is pinned; the latest compatible releases are used, which is an unverified choice on my part.
The buggy-vs-fixed transition depends on the source revision, not on any dependency pin, so no dependency is pinned to force the behaviour.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 6ce79779b18c, the new datetimelike astype tests fail: the cast to Sparse[int64]/Sparse[bool] produces the subtype default 0/False at unstored positions (or the fully dense case keeps the wrong fill_value), so sp_array_equal or dtype/to_dense assertions fail. On the fixed revision, the same selected tests pass, with the source fill_value converted to the target subtype, including fully dense arrays and pandas-spelled NaT/Timestamp/Timedelta fills.
strategy.numerical_probe: vals = np.array([1,1,2], dtype='M8[ns]'); SparseArray(vals, fill_value=np.datetime64(1,'ns')).astype('Sparse[int64]') should densify to [1,1,2] with fill_value 1 on the fixed revision, while the buggy revision gives fill 0 at unstored positions.

input_output_examples.input: vals = np.array(['2016-01-02', '2016-01-02', '2016-01-03'], dtype='M8[ns]'); arr = SparseArray(vals, fill_value=pd.Timestamp('2016-01-02'));

risks: The bug manifests as a wrong value on the buggy revision and the transition needs a successful build of that revision; if the editable build fails on the local toolchain, no transition can be observed.

Unit-less np.datetime64('NaT') triggers a NumPy DeprecationWarning; if pytest is configured to turn warnings into errors, test collection or the test itself may fail on both revisions for reasons unrelated to the bug.
Comparing SparseDtype fill values across subtypes may emit numpy timedelta64 == int deprecation warnings, which can again be escalated to errors by the project's pytest configuration.

The developer's test is parametrized over NumPy and pandas scalar spellings; the NumPy version chosen (unbounded, unverified) may change whether the numpy-spelled fills behave as the test expects, so the transition should be checked against the installed NumPy.
The fully dense case (npoints == len) and the bool case are only exercised by specific test functions; running only the -k filter that misses them would give a false pass.

The evidence does not state a platform, so no architecture-specific behaviour is assumed; a defect that only shows under another architecture or sanitiser would not transition on a standard Linux x86_64 build.

oracle.reference_source: the developer's test assertions in test_astype.py (tm.assert_sp_array_equal and dtype/to_dense equality)
oracle.why: The assertions compare integer results and SparseDtype fill values exactly, so an exact oracle is appropriate.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the cast takes the target default fill_value (0 or False) instead of converting the source datetimelike fill_value, so sp_array_equal or the dtype/to_dense equality assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the source fill_value is converted to the target subtype, so the selected tests pass.
